First assignment : document analysis and organizational synthesis
Task 1 : Inventory
I used AI to sum up the inventory, by asking all the following sections for each documents. I then sent the 31 documents to copilot and it did this tab. I didn’t succeed to understand why I only got 29 lines, for 31 documents. Because of lack of time, I decided to do the others tasks with this 29 lines inventory.

Task 3 : Synthesis divergence
Across the set of documents, we find out three main divergences. For this part, I used AI to help me underline the divergences and then I redacted my synthesis.
The first one is about optimization-centric methods. This methods helps with explaining clearly the problem, but are struggling in some fields suchas furnace deterioration or gas uncertainty. This methods provides a good precision but forces a rigidity for dynamic environments.
The second divergence is on learning driven approaches, that are offering strong responses and a multi coordination, but less transparent and are data dependent. These are adapted for complex systems but are less understandable.
Then, the last divergence is about human-centric and XAI framework. This introduce more transparency and explains the problem. Nevertheless, these models doesn’t guarantee optimality of the solutions.
Task 4 : Integrative synthesis
For the rest, due to lack of time and a bad comprehension, I relied on AI to do the synthesis, and then I checked it.
Unify insights from DRL, Digital Twins, XAI, and metallurgical constraints into a coherent operational architecture. The blueprint defines four layers: (1) Physical Metallurgical Layer capturing furnace dynamics, ladle logistics, rolling constraints, and energy profiles; (2) Digital Twin Layer providing real-time state estimation, predictive models, and virtual replicas of furnaces, mills, and dispatching systems; (3) Decision Intelligence Layer combining DRL agents for dynamic scheduling, MILP solvers for constrained optimization, and hybrid controllers for uncertainty management; (4) Explainability & Governance Layer ensuring transparency through XAI, counterfactual reasoning, human-in-loop validation, and safety protocols. Integration rules specify that DTs supply continuous state vectors to DRL agents, DRL proposes adaptive schedules, MILP validates feasibility under metallurgical limits, and XAI exposes trade-offs between energy, throughput, and robustness. The resulting blueprint aligns theoretical advances with industrial constraints, enabling a scalable, interpretable, and energy-efficient production control ecosystem.
Task 5 : Final report
This final report follow the AIDA framework :
Attention: Rising energy costs, furnace idle losses, and sub-optimal ladle and rolling coordination create structural inefficiencies across the steelmaking workflow. The current system operates with fragmented decision layers, limited transparency, and insufficient predictive control, generating avoidable consumption and variability. Interest: Recent advances in DRL, Digital Twins, and XAI demonstrate that integrated, learning-based scheduling can reduce idle energy, stabilize furnace residence times, optimize ladle rotation, and improve rolling continuity. The document set shows converging evidence that hybrid MILP-RL approaches, DT-based predictive control, and explainable optimization outperform traditional heuristics. Desire: A unified blueprint combining DRL for adaptive scheduling, DTs for real-time metallurgical constraints, and XAI for transparent decision justification provides both performance gains and organizational trust. This architecture ensures operators understand why the system acts, supervisors validate constraints, and management secures measurable reductions in energy intensity. Action: Deploy a phased roadmap: build DTs for furnaces and ladles; integrate DRL agents for scheduling and energy optimization; embed XAI modules for operator-facing transparency; run pilot loops on reheating and ladle dispatch; scale to full plant scheduling. This convergent strategy aligns technological capability with metallurgical reality and provides a clear path to measurable energy savings and operational stability.
